description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge): 3 surveys, 2 real blasts and 2 phantom ones, and 5 contract acceptances against a mine that goes formally bankrupt before the first blast ever fires -- named for a $250k win, but `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (locked) and, under #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling, the $150,000 budget can no longer fund the 12-person roster staffed:true adds through even the first drilling wait. BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized. fires at tick 132, long before blast 1 and long before the operator (per this file's own command sequence) notices or stops; see the pattern-1 drill-wait step and Findings #59-#60 for the full trajectory. Interaction-mode finding, this file's own: once levelEndReason turns non-null at tick 132, LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay (z-index 9999, every panel/toolbar control sits at z 100-200) covers the whole screen for the rest of the run and never clears -- no player click reaches ANY panel again after that tick, including blast 1's own charge/sequence/execute and every contract-accept/drill-plan-grid step that follows. Every step past tick 132 that mutates state now runs its command directly (role:'guard' + expect.blocked, same convention this file already used for its phantom blasts) instead of pretending a click still lands. #586 (issue #593's dispatch/position-sync fix): blast 1 now kills 2 (both surveyors) instead of 4 -- both driller/drill_rig pairs survive it, so pattern 2 is no longer a ghost: it drills and blasts for real, killing the 2 drillers blast 1 spared and destroying both rigs. deathCount still totals 4 by tick 900, same as the pre-#593 file, just reached via a second real blast instead of a single one; patterns 3 and 4 are the ones that are ghosts now. Final state: 4 deaths, 2 real blasts, 2 phantom patterns, 5 contract cycles, final cash -$1,381,027 (was -$1,299,912 pre-#593 -- lower now, from blast 2's own payroll/materials/event cascade running on a shifted tick schedule) -- only the UI-reachability half of each assertion, plus the numbers this second real blast actually moves, needed fixing.

steps.description: #553: sandbox-measured -- this is where the mine's math actually breaks. staffed:true's free composition adds 5 more salaried employees on top of this file's own 7 hires -- a 12-person roster costing ~$7,570 per payroll cycle (Payroll transaction, every ~10 ticks, Finance.ts) against a $150,000 budget that used to only have to fund 7. After hiring, surveying and the 3-vehicle fleet, cash sits at $3,278 -- already under BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000, balance.ts) before a single tick of this wait runs. BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100) later, 'BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.' fires at tick 132 (state.bankruptcy.bankrupt / state.levelEnded flip to true, state.levelEndReason to 'bankruptcy', Bankruptcy.ts) -- inside this very first tick chunk, long before the 2 driller/drill_rig pairs land 23 of this pattern's 24 holes by tick 440 (the 24th never lands -- a narrow #593 dispatch-timing edge case, see the charge step below) and long before blast 1 ever fires. Nothing in the engine stops a `tick` command from continuing to run a level after levelEnded flips (a genuinely pending EVENT, like the Explosive Tariff below, is the only thing that ever halts one), so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working -- for the rest of this file.

#553: resolves the Explosive Tariff event that cut this tick call short at tick 140 (108 of 150 requested) -- politics_explosive_tariff option 0 pays the $20,000 tariff in full (fixed, RNG-free delta). CI finding, this PR (#586): was role:player driving `resolveEventIfPending`'s real click -- state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 132 (8 ticks before this event pends), and the event dialog's own overlay class (`.bs-confirm-overlay`, EventModal.ts) sits at z-index 600, far below `--bsx-z-menu` (9999) that LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay has owned since tick 132 -- same class of bug as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps further down this file, just on a dialog instead of a panel, and reached earlier because this event happens to pend this late. Every other 'event choose 0' step in this drilling wait stays role:player safely because `resolveEventIfPending` no-ops (no click at all) when nothing is genuinely pending; this is the one step in the wait where an event really is pending at the moment it runs, so it is the one that actually reaches `resolveEventIfPending`'s bare `page.click('#bs-event-dialog .bs-event-choice')` -- which has no `describeUnclickable` wrapper, so Puppeteer's own unnamed 'Node is either not clickable or not an Element' surfaced instead of a diagnosis. Converted to guard + expect.blocked, command run directly so cash still drops by the tariff.
